title: Attorney General of Arkansas

context.text: Incumbent Republican Tim Griffin was unopposed in the Republican primary, which was canceled. Ballotpedia, The Green Papers and Talk Business & Politics list no Democratic, Libertarian or independent candidate for this office as of October 19, 2026.

candidates.name: Tim Griffin
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the Republican primary, which was canceled.

summary.text: Tim Griffin is the incumbent Republican Attorney General, sworn in on January 10, 2023. He previously served as Arkansas's Lieutenant Governor (2015-2023) and as the U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District (2011-2015), and is a colonel in the Arkansas Army National Guard.

background.text: Graduate of Hendrix College and Tulane Law School; attended graduate school at Oxford University.
Served as U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas and as Special Assistant to the President and Deputy Director of Political Affairs for President George W. Bush.
Served more than 28 years as a U.S. Army Reserve Judge Advocate General's Corps officer, including active duty as an Army prosecutor in 2005 with the 101st Airborne Division in Mosul, Iraq.

record.text: Joined Louisiana and Alabama in filing a civil suit against 29 defendants for shipping abortion pills into the three states, alleging violations of federal public nuisance common law and, for Arkansas, consumer-protection laws; Arkansas also joined the other two states in an original action in the U.S. Supreme Court challenging California, Massachusetts and New York shield laws, according to the Attorney General's news release.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or statement of priorities could be reached, so priorities and positions are left blank. The Attorney General's news pages loaded only once, so a single official action is listed; the release as loaded shows no date.

sources.title: Attorney General Griffin joins Louisiana and Alabama in suing 29 defendants for shipping abortion pills across state lines

researchNotes: Griffin is unopposed in November per Ballotpedia (which warns its list may not be complete), The Green Papers ("Uncontested Race") and Talk Business & Politics (no opponent drew at filing). The Arkansas Secretary of State's candidate search is a script-driven page that could not be read, so the official certified list was not checked.
